verdict.rationale: Ardent documents some deletion controls of its own: a connector deletion-lock API endpoint that blocks deletes until unlocked, and CLI-driven creation and deletion of branches. Its architecture docs also say actual data stays in the data plane, with only metadata reaching the control plane. There is no evidence of retention policies such as branch TTLs or auto-expiry, of retention windows for metadata or logs, or of a way to purge vendor-held data. missing for 10: configurable retention periods or branch expiry, documented account and data deletion and purge guarantees, metadata and log retention policy, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: Lock deletion | POST /v1/connectors/{connector_id}/deletion-lock | Blocks deletes until unlocked
